newsitem.title: USA: Major stock movements overnight - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: Major stock movements overnight - Sept 24.

text.p: NEW YORK - Stock prices soared briefly Tuesday after the Federal Reserve decided to keep interest rates steady, but the market quickly retreated as investors assessed the implications of the central bank's move.
Bonds also jumped at first before surrendering some of their gains, but the dollar drew sustained selling pressure.
Shortly after 3:40 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 40.69 points at 5,854.06 after initially gaining 35 points on the Fed's decision.

The decision surprised some Wall Street analysts who had expected the central bank to raise rates for the first time in 1-1/2 years. Prior to the Fed's decision, the Dow index had hovered around unchanged.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was up 12/32 after initially rising nearly half a point, and its yield fell to 6.99 percent from 7.02 percent at Monday's close.
Analysts said the stock market had already priced in a quarter-point rise in interest rates. Tuesday's declines came a day after the Dow set a closing record of 5,894.74.
The Fed's decision, which had been anxiously awaited on Wall Street left the key federal funds rate that banks charge each other for overnight loans unchanged at 5-1/4 percent.
The central bank also held the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks, at five percent.

LONDON - British shares extended yesterday's steep decline on Tuesday as concerns about higher U.S. interest rates sparked another wave of profit-taking, traders said. The leading FTSE 100 closed 9.2 points lower at 3,910.5, as decliners outnumbered advancers by a margin of about five to four.

FRANKFURT - German shares advanced in tentative bourse trade on Tuesday, buoyed by Wall Street's overnight gains and quietly confident that an expected U.S. rate hike later today will not exceed 25 basis points. The 30-share blue-chip DAX index ended the floor session up 11.41 points at 2,638.45. In post-bourse trade the index rose 19.24 to 2,643.42.

PARIS - French shares finished higher on Tuesday, the first day of the monthly account, but the market's advance was cautious ahead of an anticipated increase in U.S. interest rates and a string of upcoming corporate results. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 14.41 points at 2,081.50.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended higher in a technical reaction to Monday's losses and by covering of short positions, but uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting kept a lid on the market, dealers said. The all-share SPI added 14.81 points to 2,349.09.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended mixed on Tuesday, with most participants sidelined on the last trading day for September delivery and ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting scheduled for later today. Brokers said the sluggish trade may continue for a while. The key Nikkei 225 average closed up 59.75 points at 21,171.99.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended near session lows on Tuesday, weighed down by caution ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting later today and share placements from Henderson Land and COSCO Pacific. The Hang Seng index closed 75.43 points lower at 11,546.70 after falling to a low of 11,538.76.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed higher on Tuesday, keeping a firm grasp on gains that had looked unlikely at the start of the day. By the close, the All Ordinaries index was up 9.5 points at 2228.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks were closed on Tuesday for a market holiday. On Monday the overall index shed 17.4 points to 6,917.9 points, the industrial index was down 19.9 points to 8,170.9 points and the gold index fell 16.5 points to 1,721.4 points.
